inline_comments.comment: Per project convention, the first word of the description following the commit-type prefix must be capitalized. Change `implement` to `Implement`: `feat: Implement neo look styling for mindmap diagrams`.

The `looks` array is `['neo'] as const` — a single-element array. The outer `looks.forEach` loop therefore runs exactly once and adds no generality; `look` is always `'neo'`. Consider removing the outer loop and hardcoding `look` at the `imgSnapshotTest` call site, or documenting why this wrapping structure is intentional (e.g., to make it easy to add `'classic'` in future).

Per project rules, the `default` case in a `switch` statement must call `log.error(...)` or throw an error rather than silently returning a value. The current `return label` silently swallows any unrecognized shape. Since this is a test helper with a closed `mindmapShapes` tuple, a throw is the right guard:
```typescript
default:
  throw new Error(`Unknown mindmap shape: ${shape}`);
```

`getConfig()` is called at the top of `flattenNodes`, which is a recursive function — it calls `this.flattenNodes(child, processedNodes)` for every child node. This violates the project rule: *"Never call `getConfig()` inside recursive or shared helper functions where it would be re-invoked on every recursion."* For a large mindmap tree, `getConfig()` executes once per node. Move the call to the non-recursive entry point (e.g., `getData()`) and pass `conf` as a parameter down to `flattenNodes`.

Same issue as `flattenNodes`: `getConfig()` is called at the top of `generateEdges`, which is also recursive — the loop body calls `this.generateEdges(child, edges)`. `getConfig()` therefore executes once per node. Pass `conf` as a parameter from the non-recursive caller instead of re-fetching it on every frame of the recursion.

The neo-specific CSS selectors are very long single-line strings that exceed any reasonable line-length limit and are difficult to read or diff. For example:
```
[data-look="neo"].mindmap-node.section-${i - 1} rect, [data-look="neo"].mindmap-node.section-${i - 1} path, ...
```
Consider extracting the repeated prefix into a template variable and breaking the selector list across lines:
```typescript
const sel = `[data-look="neo"].mindmap-node.section-${i - 1}`;
sections += `
  ${sel} rect,
  ${sel} path,
  ${sel} circle,
  ${sel} polygon { ... }
`;
```

This is a cosmetic-only whitespace change to `dropShadow` (`'drop-shadow( 1px ..., rgba(185,185,185,1))'` → `'drop-shadow(1px ..., rgba(185, 185, 185, 1))'`). While the two values are CSS-equivalent, modifying any shared theme variable in `theme-default.js` requires verifying the rendered appearance across all five built-in themes before merging per project rules. Additionally, unrelated cosmetic fixes mixed into a feature PR make the diff harder to review. Consider moving this to a dedicated clean-up PR.

general_comments.comment: The neo-specific colour ternaries in `genSections` and `getStyles` are inconsistently grouped across the three CSS properties they control (fill, stroke, text colour). For example, `neutral` is included alongside redux themes in the fill rule (`fill: ... theme === 'neutral' ? options.mainBkg : ...`) but is absent from the edge stroke rule (`stroke: theme?.includes('redux') || theme === 'neo-dark' ? options.nodeBorder : ...`). This means nodes in the neutral theme receive `mainBkg` fill but a section-scale stroke colour, likely producing a visual mismatch. Centralise the per-theme colour decisions into a small helper that returns `{ fill, stroke, labelColor }` based on theme, then reference it consistently in all three rules.

In the Cypress test, the grandchildren are all appended at 6-space indentation, which in mindmap's indentation-driven syntax means they become children of the **last** 4-space-indented node (`n4`, the bang shape), not of their respective parents. The comment says *"Add grandchildren to each child with different shapes"* but the generated tree does not match that description — all grandchildren end up under one parent. While the snapshot may still serve as a useful visual regression fixture, the misleading comment should be corrected to accurately describe the actual tree structure produced.

The `genSections` helper destructures `const { theme, look } = options;` at its top level, but `options` is typed as `any` and declared optional (`options?: any`) in the `DiagramStylesProvider` signature. If `options` is `undefined`, the destructuring throws a `TypeError` at runtime. Although `genSections` is only called internally from `getStyles` (which always supplies `options`), the type contract doesn't enforce this. Adding an early-return guard (`if (!options) return '';`) or narrowing the internal helper's parameter type would make the contract explicit and safe.
